PullRequest.Title: Add explicit Responses API prompt caching
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- add explicit prompt cache breakpoint placement for supported Responses API models
- retain two stable prefix anchors and the latest 20 conversation boundaries
- support GPT-5.6 variants and GPT-6 models, including GPT-6 Astra
- enable explicit prompt caching by default for supported models

## Testing
- npm run test:unit -- src/extension/intents/node/test/cacheBreakpoints.spec.ts src/platform/endpoint/node/test/responsesApi.spec.ts
- 85 tests passed

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The default flip, global serializer gate, sole production marker-insertion call, and repeated Inline Chat request path are directly traced. The exact provider-side latency varies with prompt size and cache residency, but explicit mode without any markers necessarily removes the prior implicit-cache opportunity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: uncached server-side prompt-token processing on existing Responses API calls
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The wasted processing scales with the stable prompt prefix size multiplied by the number of non-agent tool-loop requests; Inline Chat permits more than nine read-only rounds and rerenders the growing previous-round history each time.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased latency and repeated server compute for multi-round non-agent requests
Findings.PreviousBehavior: With this setting defaulting to false, supported Responses models used `prompt_cache_options: { mode: 'implicit' }`, so requests that did not contain explicit markers could still use automatic prompt caching.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new true default makes `createResponsesRequestBody` select explicit mode for every GPT-5.6/GPT-6 Responses request, even when its messages contain no cache-breakpoint parts.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Changing the contributed setting default from `false` to `true` at line 4097 activates explicit mode by default for all supported Responses requests; no corresponding marker insertion was added to non-Agent request builders.
Findings.Title: Keep implicit caching when no breakpoints were inserted
Findings.Impact: Inline Chat and other non-Agent callers using GPT-5.6/GPT-6 send no explicit breakpoints. Their repeated tool-loop requests now reprocess the unchanged system/file/history prefix instead of receiving implicit cache hits, increasing response latency as the prompt and round count grow.
Findings.Evidence: `createResponsesRequestBody` reads this setting globally and selects explicit mode solely from the setting plus model support (`responsesApi.ts:131-153`), not from request location or the presence of a marker. The only production call to `addCacheBreakpoints` is in `AgentIntentInvocation` (`agentIntent.ts:1050-1052`). In contrast, Inline Chat directly calls `makeChatRequest2` with rendered messages (`inlineChatIntent.ts:450`) inside a loop that appends `previousRounds` and allows more than nine read-only rounds (`inlineChatIntent.ts:293-383`), without inserting markers. The serializer attaches `prompt_cache_breakpoint` only when a `CacheBreakpoint` part is present (`responsesApi.ts:634-645`), so these explicit-mode requests contain no cache anchors.
Findings.Recommendation: Select explicit mode only when the serialized request actually contains at least one explicit breakpoint (or gate it to the Agent path); otherwise retain implicit mode. Alternatively, wire marker insertion into every supported request builder before enabling the default globally.

Scenarios.Scenario: Multi-round Agent request on a supported GPT-5.6/GPT-6 Responses model
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Prompt rendering, breakpoint reconstruction, request-body serialization, and one Responses API network call must complete for each agent iteration. Breakpoint scanning is synchronous but linear in the already-rendered prompt; the network response dominates the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and send one Responses API model request per agent/tool-loop iteration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model call per sequential iteration; marker count is bounded to twenty-two after grouping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same model call occurred per iteration, but explicit caching defaulted off and the Responses strategy used at most the shared four-marker placement when enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each call is the main response-latency boundary; explicit cache hits can reduce processing of stable prompt prefixes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rendered messages and content parts across conversation turns/tool rounds; the algorithm scans the full rendered prompt and retains at most two prefix plus twenty conversation markers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Agent tool rounds are sequential model requests; tools within a round may execute concurrently, but no new network-call burst or limiter change is introduced here.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The first request or a changed prefix is cold. Stable system/global-context anchors and the latest twenty user/tool boundaries allow later iterations to hit explicit cache entries. Markers are rebuilt idempotently each render; there is no client-side retained cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the changed marker placement is linear and bounded, and that it does not add boundary calls or concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider cache-hit duration and user prompt sizes vary, but the bounded local scans are small relative to request serialization and model latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression in the intended Agent scenario; the added local work is bounded and supports reduced remote prompt processing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Multi-round Inline Chat tool loop on a supported GPT-5.6/GPT-6 Responses model
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each iteration rerenders the prompt with prior rounds, serializes it, sends a Responses API request, waits for the response, and executes tools before the next iteration. The model call is on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send a Responses API request for each inline-edit tool round.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential call per round; the loop permits more than nine read-only rounds and up to five failed-edit retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Call count was identical, but supported models used implicit prompt caching by default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Every call blocks progress, and loss of implicit cache reuse causes the stable prompt prefix to be processed again on subsequent calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Select explicit cache mode and serialize markers only when CacheBreakpoint parts exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per model request; zero markers for Inline Chat because only AgentIntent inserts them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The false setting default selected implicit mode for the same marker-free body.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The serialization choice disables the prior implicit cache opportunity before the existing network boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Stable system/file context plus the growing previous-round history, multiplied by up to more than nine read-only rounds and additional failed-edit retries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model requests are sequential across rounds. Tool executions within a round use Promise.allSettled, but that does not coalesce or overlap the next model request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Before the default flip, these marker-free requests selected implicit caching. Afterward they select explicit mode by default, but Inline Chat never invokes addCacheBreakpoints, so cold behavior repeats and there are no explicit anchors to become warm.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high confidence from the global mode gate, sole production marker-insertion call, and traced Inline Chat loop.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depends on provider cache policy, prompt token count, and number of rounds, but the mode change and absence of markers are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cache-lifecycle regression: default explicit mode is applied to a repeated non-Agent request path that supplies no explicit breakpoints.

Scenarios.Scenario: Unsupported-model or explicitly disabled Responses request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Prompt rendering and request serialization precede the existing Responses API call. Agent rendering still reconstructs markers, but serialization drops them when the model/setting gate is false.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the existing Responses API request without explicit markers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same network request and unsupported-model behavior existed before the change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No diff-introduced network fan-out; unsupported models preserve prior request mode.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rendered message/content count; no serialized marker count and no additional boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unsupported models omit prompt_cache_options; supported models with the setting disabled retain implicit mode. No client cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the local work occurs but is not a concrete reportable regression at realistic prompt sizes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The extra Agent-side full-prompt marker reconstruction for unsupported models is linear and allocates temporary arrays, but no evidence shows material latency relative to rendering/network work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding; the added marker preprocessing is bounded and does not alter expensive-boundary cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and traced Agent, Inline Chat, serializer, model-gating, and tool-loop paths. Submitted one medium cache-lifecycle finding for globally enabling explicit mode on marker-free non-Agent requests. No boundary fan-out, unbounded retention, concurrency burst, or material serialization/allocation regression was otherwise established.
